statement: The system shall require two-factor authentication using two of a knowledge factor, a biometric and a hard token to sign a controlled-substance prescription.
sources: F-PRES-03: I will not use a fingerprint reader; I will use a password and a hard token. || F-SEC-02: I would prefer every prescriber to use a biometric factor with the hard token. || DOC-IDP

statement: The system shall accept as a hard token only a device separate from the workstation that is validated to FIPS 140-2 Security Level 1 or higher.
sources: F-SEC-01: Hard tokens must be separate devices validated to at least FIPS 140-2 Security Level 1. || DOC-VENDOR

statement: The system shall allow a prescriber to sign with a password and a hard token without using a biometric factor.
sources: F-PRES-03: I will not use a fingerprint reader; I will use a password and a hard token. || DOC-KICKOFF

statement: The system shall complete the signing step, including two-factor authentication, within 20 seconds for 95% of signings.
sources: F-PRES-01: Signing a controlled prescription, including the two-factor step, must take no more than 20 seconds. || DOC-KICKOFF
llm_note: 'For 95% of signings' is not in F-PRES-01, which says 'no more than 20 seconds'.

statement: The system shall limit a single signing action to controlled-substance prescriptions for one patient.
sources: F-SEC-03: Each signing action must cover prescriptions for a single patient only.

statement: The system shall display the DEA attestation statement with the prescription details while prompting for two-factor authentication.
sources: F-COMP-04: The signing screen must show the DEA-required attestation statement while the prescription details are displayed.

statement: The system shall require the practitioner to indicate that each controlled-substance prescription is ready for signing before the signing prompt is shown.
sources: F-COMP-04: The signing screen must show the DEA-required attestation statement while the prescription details are displayed.
llm_note: The cited F-COMP-04 does not mention an indication of readiness; the support is the control, 21 CFR 1311.120(b)(9)-(11).

statement: The system shall allow only the practitioner whose DEA registration number appears on a prescription to sign it.
sources: DOC-FINDING

statement: The system shall require the practitioner to select the DEA registration number to place on the prescription when the practitioner holds more than one.
sources: F-PRES-04: When I hold more than one DEA registration, I must be asked which one goes on the prescription. || DOC-CRED

statement: The system shall time- and date-stamp each controlled-substance prescription when it is signed.
sources: F-COMP-04: The signing screen must show the DEA-required attestation statement while the prescription details are displayed.
llm_note: The cited F-COMP-04 does not mention a time stamp; the support is the control, 21 CFR 1311.120(b)(14)-(16).

statement: The system shall digitally sign the required prescription information and archive the digitally signed record.
sources: F-PHARM-01: Every controlled prescription must arrive with an indication that the prescribing practitioner signed it.
llm_note: The cited F-PHARM-01 asks for a signed indication, not digital signing and archiving; the support is the control.

statement: The system shall store the application's private signing key encrypted in a FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic module.
sources: F-SEC-04: The private signing key must be stored encrypted in a FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic module.

statement: The system shall cancel a controlled-substance prescription if any required information is altered after it has been signed.
sources: F-PHARM-03: Any change to the prescription content in transit must make it invalid.
llm_note: The cited F-PHARM-03 is about changes in transit; alteration after signing comes from the control, 1311.120(b)(19).

statement: The system shall keep application time within five minutes of the official NIST time source.
sources: F-SEC-05: Application time must stay within five minutes of the NIST time source.

statement: The system shall require each grant or revocation of signing access to be entered by one designated individual.
sources: F-COMP-01: Granting or revoking signing access must be entered by one designated person and approved by a second designated person who is a DEA registrant using two-factor authentication. || DOC-CRED
llm_note: 1311.125 governs individual practitioners. A hospital credentialing office falls under 1311.130 (in the corpus, not in the control catalogue).

statement: The system shall require a second designated individual who is a DEA registrant to approve each signing-access change using two-factor authentication.
sources: F-COMP-01: Granting or revoking signing access must be entered by one designated person and approved by a second designated person who is a DEA registrant using two-factor authentication. || DOC-CRED
llm_note: As G-EPCS-15: 1311.130 has the list approved by two individuals and entered separately, which is what DOC-CRED describes.

statement: The system shall revoke a practitioner's signing access on the same day a lost token or lapsed registration is reported.
sources: F-CRED-03: Signing access must be revoked on the same day we learn a token is lost or a registration has lapsed. || DOC-FINDING || DOC-VENDOR
llm_note: The audit finding also requires revocation on the day a practitioner leaves; that trigger is missing.

statement: The system shall remove signing permission within 15 minutes of receiving a revocation event from the identity provider.
sources: DOC-IDP

statement: The system shall record every identity-proofing event and every credential issued.
sources: F-CRED-04: We must keep a record of every identity proofing and every credential issued. || DOC-CRED
llm_note: 1311.105 is for external credential providers; in-house proofing is 1311.110 (in the corpus, not in the catalogue).

statement: The credentialing process shall verify government photographic ID, state licence and DEA registration before a signing credential is issued.
sources: F-CRED-01: The credentialing office verifies government photo ID, state licence and DEA registration before a practitioner's credential is issued. || DOC-CRED
llm_note: As G-EPCS-19: the applicable section looks like 1311.110, not 1311.105.

statement: The system shall issue credential activation information through two separate channels.
sources: DOC-CRED
llm_note: As G-EPCS-19 for the cited control.

statement: The system shall include an indication that the prescribing practitioner signed the prescription in every transmitted controlled-substance prescription.
sources: F-PHARM-01: Every controlled prescription must arrive with an indication that the prescribing practitioner signed it.

statement: The system shall transmit a signed controlled-substance prescription to the pharmacy without converting it to facsimile or any other form.
sources: F-PHARM-02: A prescription must never reach us as a fax converted from the electronic original.

statement: The system shall treat any alteration of prescription content during transmission as invalidating the prescription.
sources: F-PHARM-03: Any change to the prescription content in transit must make it invalid.

statement: The system shall allow a manually signed replacement to be printed only after a failed-transmission notice, stating the pharmacy and the date and time of the failed transmission.
sources: F-PRES-05: If the pharmacy does not receive the prescription, I need to be told and be able to print a manually signed replacement that says the electronic transmission failed.
llm_note: Covers the printed replacement; telling the prescriber that transmission failed (F-PRES-05) is not a requirement of its own.

statement: The system shall record in each audit record the date and time, the event type, the identity of the person acting and the outcome.
sources: F-AUD-04: Audit records must record date and time, event type, the person acting and the outcome, and must not be modifiable. || DOC-FINDING

statement: The system shall protect audit records from modification and deletion.
sources: F-AUD-04: Audit records must record date and time, event type, the person acting and the outcome, and must not be modifiable.

statement: The system shall analyse the audit trail every calendar day and generate an incident report of auditable events.
sources: F-AUD-01: The audit trail must be analysed every calendar day and an incident report produced for each auditable event.

statement: The organisation shall report security incidents affecting prescription records to the DEA within one business day.
sources: F-AUD-02: Suspected security incidents affecting prescription records must be reported to the DEA within one business day.

statement: The system shall give each practitioner a log of the previous month's controlled-substance prescriptions within seven days of month end, sortable by patient, drug and date of issuance.
sources: F-AUD-03: Each practitioner must receive a log of the previous month's controlled prescriptions within seven days of month end, sortable by patient, drug and date.

statement: The system shall retain controlled-substance records electronically for two years in a readily retrievable form.
sources: F-COMP-03: Controlled-substance records must be retained electronically for two years and be readily retrievable.

statement: The application shall pass a third-party EPCS audit before it is used for controlled-substance prescriptions.
sources: F-COMP-02: The application may not be used for controlled substances until the third-party audit has passed, and it must be re-audited whenever signing functionality changes or every two years. || DOC-KICKOFF

statement: The application shall be re-audited whenever signing functionality changes or every two years, whichever comes first.
sources: F-COMP-02: The application may not be used for controlled substances until the third-party audit has passed, and it must be re-audited whenever signing functionality changes or every two years.

statement: The system shall use mutual TLS for all calls between the application and the identity provider.
sources: DOC-IDP

statement: The system shall not accept the workforce single sign-on session as a signing factor.
sources: DOC-IDP

statement: The system shall display drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction alerts before a medication order can be signed.
sources: F-PRES-01: Interaction and allergy alerts must appear before I can sign the order, not after it has gone to the pharmacy. || F-COMP-01: The module must be certified against the ONC criteria for CPOE medications, drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checks, and electronic prescribing before go-live.

statement: The system shall return the interaction and allergy check result within 2 seconds for at least 95% of orders at a load of 1,200 orders per hour.
sources: F-PRES-02: The interaction and allergy check must come back within 2 seconds for at least 95% of orders; past 5 seconds prescribers start working around it. || F-ARCH-05: Peak load is 1,200 orders per hour across the network.
llm_note: Merges two sources: the 1,200 orders/hour load comes from the architect, the 2 s target from the prescriber. Neither states them together.

statement: The system shall interrupt ordering only for high-severity interaction alerts and show moderate-severity interactions as non-blocking notices.
sources: F-PRES-06: Only high-severity interactions should interrupt ordering; moderate ones should show as a non-blocking notice. || DOC-INCIDENT

statement: The system shall block signing when an order matches an allergy recorded with high criticality until the prescriber acknowledges the alert.
sources: F-CSO-01: A drug-allergy match against an allergy recorded with high criticality must block signing until the prescriber acknowledges it.

statement: The system shall require a reason selected from a coded list for every override of an interaction or allergy alert.
sources: F-CSO-02: Every override of an interaction or allergy alert must record a reason chosen from a coded list, plus free text for high-severity alerts. || DOC-POLICY || DOC-INCIDENT
llm_note: Covers interaction and allergy alerts only; the incident report also asks for a reason on duplicate-therapy overrides.

statement: The system shall require a free-text justification in addition to the coded reason when a high-severity alert is overridden.
sources: F-CSO-02: Every override of an interaction or allergy alert must record a reason chosen from a coded list, plus free text for high-severity alerts.

statement: The system shall transmit the alert override reason with the prescription to the dispensing pharmacy.
sources: F-PHARM-02: When a prescriber overrides an interaction alert, the override reason must travel with the prescription so we can decide whether to call them. || DOC-INCIDENT

statement: The system shall restrict changes to interaction severity levels to administrators appointed by the pharmacy and therapeutics committee.
sources: F-CSO-03: Only administrators appointed by the pharmacy and therapeutics committee may change interaction severity levels.

statement: The system shall produce a monthly report of alert overrides grouped by prescriber and drug pair.
sources: F-CSO-04: A monthly report of all alert overrides, broken down by prescriber and drug pair, must be produced for the safety committee.

statement: The system shall display the interaction knowledge-base version on every alert.
sources: F-CSO-05: The interaction knowledge base must be updated at least monthly, and its version must be shown on every alert.

statement: The interaction knowledge base shall be updated at least once a month.
sources: F-CSO-05: The interaction knowledge base must be updated at least monthly, and its version must be shown on every alert.

statement: The system shall display the patient's active medication list and recorded allergies on the order entry screen.
sources: F-PRES-04: The patient's active medication list and recorded allergies must be visible on the same screen as the order I am writing.

statement: The system shall flag duplicate therapy, two active orders in the same therapeutic class, to the prescriber before signing.
sources: DOC-POLICY || DOC-INCIDENT
llm_note: Flagging is covered; the incident report's override reason for duplicate therapy is not.

statement: The system shall require verification by a second licensed clinician before a high-alert medication prescription is transmitted.
sources: DOC-POLICY

statement: The system shall prevent transmission of a prescription that lacks the drug name, strength, dose form, quantity, directions for use or number of refills.
sources: F-PHARM-01: Every prescription must arrive with drug name, strength, dose form, quantity, directions for use and the number of refills authorised. || DOC-EMAIL

statement: The system shall require the prescriber to state on each prescription whether generic substitution is permitted.
sources: F-PHARM-04: Each prescription must state explicitly whether generic substitution is permitted. || DOC-EMAIL

statement: The system shall accept oral liquid medication quantities in millilitres only.
sources: F-PHARM-05: Oral liquid medications must be prescribed in millilitres only.

statement: The system shall send new prescriptions to the e-prescribing intermediary as NCPDP SCRIPT NewRx messages.
sources: F-ARCH-02: Pharmacy transmission goes through the existing intermediary using NCPDP SCRIPT NewRx, RxChangeRequest, CancelRx and RxRenewalRequest messages. || DOC-INTERFACE

statement: The system shall allow a prescriber to cancel a transmitted prescription by sending a CancelRx message to the pharmacy.
sources: F-PRES-07: I need to change or cancel a prescription that has already been sent, and the pharmacy must be notified electronically. || F-PHARM-03: Cancellations must reach the pharmacy as an electronic CancelRx message and the pharmacy's response must be shown to the prescriber. || DOC-EMAIL

statement: The system shall display the pharmacy's response to each cancellation request to the prescriber.
sources: F-PHARM-03: Cancellations must reach the pharmacy as an electronic CancelRx message and the pharmacy's response must be shown to the prescriber. || DOC-EMAIL

statement: The system shall allow a prescriber to change a transmitted prescription through an RxChangeRequest message.
sources: F-PRES-07: I need to change or cancel a prescription that has already been sent, and the pharmacy must be notified electronically. || F-ARCH-02: Pharmacy transmission goes through the existing intermediary using NCPDP SCRIPT NewRx, RxChangeRequest, CancelRx and RxRenewalRequest messages.

statement: The system shall notify the prescriber within 60 seconds when transmission of a prescription to the pharmacy fails.
sources: F-PRES-05: If transmission to the pharmacy fails I need to be told within 60 seconds, and be able to resend or pick another pharmacy.

statement: The system shall allow the prescriber to resend a failed prescription or send it to another pharmacy.
sources: F-PRES-05: If transmission to the pharmacy fails I need to be told within 60 seconds, and be able to resend or pick another pharmacy.

statement: The system shall route every pharmacy renewal request to the prescriber for review before it can be approved.
sources: F-CSO-06: No renewal request may be approved without a prescriber reviewing it.

statement: The system shall check the payer formulary for each medication order.
sources: F-ARCH-04: Formulary checks call the payer formulary service; if it does not answer within 3 seconds, ordering continues with a "formulary unavailable" notice.

statement: The system shall let ordering continue with a formulary-unavailable notice when the formulary service does not respond within 3 seconds.
sources: F-ARCH-04: Formulary checks call the payer formulary service; if it does not answer within 3 seconds, ordering continues with a "formulary unavailable" notice.

statement: The system shall publish each order received over the HL7 v2 interface as a FHIR R4 MedicationRequest.
sources: F-ARCH-01: The EHR exchanges orders over HL7 v2; the new module must publish each order as a FHIR R4 MedicationRequest through an adapter. || DOC-INTERFACE

statement: The adapter shall acknowledge an HL7 v2 order message only after the corresponding MedicationRequest has been persisted.
sources: DOC-INTERFACE

statement: The system shall achieve at least 99.9% monthly availability, excluding planned maintenance on Sundays between 02:00 and 04:00.
sources: F-ARCH-03: Availability must be at least 99.9% per month, with planned maintenance only on Sundays between 02:00 and 04:00.

statement: The system shall reach the e-prescribing intermediary acknowledgement within 10 seconds of signing for 95% of prescriptions.
sources: DOC-INTERFACE

statement: The system shall require a unique user account for every user.
sources: F-SEC-01: Every user must have a unique account; shared logins are prohibited.

statement: The system shall lock a session after 15 minutes of inactivity and require re-authentication to resume it.
sources: F-SEC-02: Sessions must lock after 15 minutes of inactivity and require re-authentication to resume.

statement: The system shall encrypt all prescription traffic to the e-prescribing intermediary with TLS 1.2 or higher.
sources: F-SEC-03: All prescription traffic to the pharmacy intermediary must be encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher and integrity-protected. || DOC-INTERFACE
llm_note: Omits the integrity protection in F-SEC-03 and the mutual TLS in DOC-INTERFACE.

statement: The system shall record auditable actions on prescriptions in tamper-evident audit records that no application user can delete.
sources: F-SEC-04: Audit records must be tamper-evident and no application user may delete them.

statement: The system shall provide break-glass emergency access to on-call clinicians.
sources: F-SEC-05: Emergency break-glass access must be available to on-call clinicians, and every use must be reviewed within 24 hours.

statement: The system shall queue every use of break-glass access for review within 24 hours.
sources: F-SEC-05: Emergency break-glass access must be available to on-call clinicians, and every use must be reviewed within 24 hours.

statement: The system shall restrict access to a patient's medication data to members of the patient's care team.
sources: F-COMP-03: Access to a patient's medication data is limited to the patient's care team; any access outside it must be logged and reviewed.

statement: The system shall log every access to a patient's medication data by a user outside the patient's care team for review.
sources: F-COMP-03: Access to a patient's medication data is limited to the patient's care team; any access outside it must be logged and reviewed.

statement: The system shall retain audit logs and security documentation for at least 6 years.
sources: F-COMP-02: Audit logs and security documentation must be retained for at least 6 years.

statement: The system shall allow a prescriber to complete a routine prescription in under 90 seconds.
sources: F-PO-03: A prescriber must be able to complete a routine prescription in under 90 seconds.

statement: The system shall identify the patient by full name and date of birth on every prescription.
sources: DOC-POLICY

statement: The system shall require a weight recorded within the last 30 days before a weight-based dose is prescribed for a patient under 18.
sources: DOC-POLICY

statement: The system shall allow trainees to draft orders that only a supervising prescriber can sign.
sources: DOC-POLICY

statement: The e-prescribing module shall be certified against ONC criteria 170.315(a)(1), (a)(4) and (b)(3) before go-live.
sources: F-COMP-01: The module must be certified against the ONC criteria for CPOE medications, drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checks, and electronic prescribing before go-live. || DOC-KICKOFF

statement: The programme shall eliminate faxed and paper outpatient prescriptions at all four hospitals within 12 months of go-live.
sources: F-PO-01: The goal is to eliminate faxed and paper outpatient prescriptions at all four hospitals within 12 months of go-live. || DOC-KICKOFF

statement: The app shall send a refill reminder 7 days before a medication's supply is expected to run out.
sources: F-PAT-01: I want a reminder 7 days before any of my medications runs out. || DOC-SURVEY

statement: The app shall calculate the run-out date from the dispensed quantity and expected supply duration of the active prescription.
sources: DOC-API

statement: The app shall let the patient start a renewal request directly from the reminder.
sources: F-PAT-03: I want to request a renewal with one tap from the reminder.

statement: The app shall require the patient to confirm they are still taking the medication before a renewal request is sent.
sources: F-PRES-01: A renewal request must only be sent after the patient confirms they are still taking the medication.

statement: The app shall not submit a renewal request without an explicit action by the patient or an authorised proxy.
sources: F-PRES-01: A renewal request must only be sent after the patient confirms they are still taking the medication. || F-PO-01: When a patient's supply runs out, the app should submit the renewal request automatically without asking the patient.

statement: The app shall deliver each renewal request to the prescriber's EHR renewal queue as a renewal-request Task.
sources: F-PRES-02: Renewal requests must arrive in my existing EHR renewal queue, not as a separate message stream. || DOC-API

statement: The app shall show a renewal as approved only after the prescriber has approved it in the EHR.
sources: F-PRES-03: The app must never tell a patient a renewal is approved until I have approved it in the EHR.

statement: The app shall show the patient the status of each renewal request.
sources: DOC-SURVEY

statement: The app shall notify the patient when the pharmacy has dispensed the medication and it is ready to collect.
sources: F-PAT-04: I want to be told when the pharmacy has my medication ready to collect. || DOC-REVIEWS || DOC-API

statement: The app shall exclude medication names and all other health information from lock-screen notifications.
sources: F-SEC-01: Lock-screen notifications must not show medication names or any other health information.

statement: The app shall show the name of the medication in a reminder only after the user has unlocked the app.
sources: F-PAT-02: The reminder should name the medication so I know which one to reorder. || F-SEC-01: Lock-screen notifications must not show medication names or any other health information.

statement: The app shall remove all health information from the device when the user logs out.
sources: F-SEC-02: The app must not keep health information on the phone after the user logs out, and anything cached while logged in must be encrypted.

statement: The app shall encrypt any health information cached on the device while the user is logged in.
sources: F-SEC-02: The app must not keep health information on the phone after the user logs out, and anything cached while logged in must be encrypted.

statement: The app shall lock after 5 minutes in the background and require biometric or PIN unlock to resume.
sources: F-SEC-04: The app must lock after 5 minutes in the background and require biometric or PIN unlock. || DOC-REVIEWS
llm_note: Cites DOC-REVIEWS as support, but that review complains about being logged out on every app switch, so it pulls the other way.

statement: The app shall authenticate patients through the network's OpenID Connect provider.
sources: F-SEC-03: Patients sign in through the network's OpenID Connect provider, with multi-factor authentication at enrolment on a new device. || DOC-API

statement: The app shall require multi-factor authentication when a patient enrols a new device.
sources: F-SEC-03: Patients sign in through the network's OpenID Connect provider, with multi-factor authentication at enrolment on a new device.

statement: The app shall let a caregiver view reminders and request renewals for a patient only while the patient's recorded consent is in force.
sources: F-CARE-01: I need to see my mother's reminders and request renewals for her, but only if she has given consent in the app. || DOC-PROXY || DOC-SURVEY

statement: The app shall record, for each proxy consent, who the proxy is, what they may do and when consent was given.
sources: DOC-PROXY

statement: The app shall let the patient revoke a caregiver's access at any time, with immediate effect.
sources: F-CARE-02: My mother must be able to withdraw my access at any time, and it must stop immediately. || DOC-PROXY

statement: The app shall require a caregiver to act under their own login and never with the patient's credentials.
sources: DOC-PROXY || DOC-REVIEWS

statement: The app shall record every action a caregiver takes against the caregiver's own identity.
sources: DOC-PROXY || DOC-API

statement: The app shall load every screen of the feature within 1 second on a mid-range phone over 4G.
sources: F-PO-02: Every screen of the feature must load within 1 second on a mid-range phone over 4G.

statement: The app shall render all feature text legibly at the largest system font size.
sources: F-PAT-05: The text must be readable at large font sizes; I use the largest setting on my phone. || DOC-SURVEY || DOC-REVIEWS

statement: The app shall support A/B testing of reminder wording.
sources: F-PO-03: We release weekly and will change reminder timing and wording based on patient feedback; the feature must support A/B testing of reminder wording.

statement: The feature shall reach renewal-request use by 30% of eligible patients within six months of launch.
sources: F-PO-04: Success means 30% of eligible patients using renewal requests within six months.

statement: The app shall stay within the gateway rate limit of 60 requests per minute per user.
sources: DOC-API

statement: The app shall send health information only to the network's FHIR API gateway.
sources: DOC-API
llm_note: An inference: DOC-API lists the gateway but does not say it is the only permitted destination.

statement: The app shall encrypt all traffic between the app and the FHIR API gateway.
sources: control:HIPAA-164.312(e)(1)
